name: International Journal of Modern Medicine & Surgery
tagline: Peer-reviewed, open-access research across medicine and surgery.
about: IJMMS publishes original research, reviews, case reports and short communications across medical and surgical specialties. All published articles are freely available to read and download.

faq:
Who can submit? | Researchers, clinicians and students in any medical or surgical field. All authors must approve the submission.
How do I submit? | Register as an author, then use Submit Manuscript. Your submission appears on your dashboard where you can follow its status.
Which article types are accepted? | Original research, systematic reviews, review articles, case reports, short communications and letters to the editor. See Author Guidelines for limits.
Is the journal open access? | Yes. Articles are free to read and download under the licence shown on each article.
How are articles cited? | Each article page shows ready-made Vancouver and APA citations with its DOI.
ethics:
IJMMS follows the recommendations of the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE) and the core practices of the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE).

Authorship: all listed authors must meet ICMJE authorship criteria and approve the final manuscript. Changes in authorship after submission need written consent from every author.

Ethics approval and consent: studies on humans need approval from an institutional ethics committee and informed consent; animal studies need institutional animal ethics approval. Clinical trials must be registered (for India, the CTRI) before enrolment.

Conflicts of interest and funding: authors, reviewers and editors must disclose financial and non-financial conflicts and all sources of funding.

Originality: manuscripts must be original, not under consideration elsewhere, and are screened with similarity-checking software before review. Duplicate publication, fabrication, falsification and plagiarism lead to rejection or retraction.

Corrections and retractions: errors are corrected through a published correction; seriously flawed or unethical work is retracted following COPE guidance.
aipolicy: Authors must disclose any use of generative AI or AI-assisted tools in preparing a manuscript (what tool, and for what purpose). AI tools cannot be listed as authors and authors remain fully responsible for the content, including accuracy of references. Reviewers and editors must not upload confidential manuscripts to public AI tools.
peer:
Every submission is screened by the editorial office for scope, ethics statements and similarity. Suitable manuscripts undergo double-blind peer review by two independent reviewers: authors and reviewers are not told each other's identity. Reviewers submit a recommendation (accept, minor revision, major revision or reject) with comments to the author. The editor makes the final decision. Reviewers must declare conflicts of interest and treat manuscripts as confidential.
A first decision is normally communicated within 2-3 weeks of submission, and accepted articles are published within 2 weeks of acceptance.
aims:
The International Journal of Modern Medicine & Surgery (IJMMS) publishes peer-reviewed research that advances clinical practice and understanding of disease across medicine and surgery.

Objectives: to provide a rigorous, freely accessible platform for original research, systematic reviews, review articles, case reports and short communications; to encourage ethical, well-reported studies that follow international reporting guidelines (CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, CARE); and to give clinicians, researchers and students dependable evidence for patient care and teaching.

Scope: clinical and translational studies, surgical techniques and outcomes, anaesthesia and critical care, pharmacology and therapeutics, diagnostics, public health, medical education and health-system research.

plag: All submissions are checked for textual similarity with similarity-detection software before peer review. Manuscripts with unacceptable overlap, duplicate publication or unattributed text are returned to the authors or rejected. Confirmed misconduct after publication is handled by correction or retraction following COPE guidance.
